## TL;DR

The latest handoff failure reported a timeout in `handoff-unification.test.ts` while waiting for a fake agent turn to end. I reran that exact test; it passed in 2.7 seconds. The branch was clean and landable, with the earlier foreign #1075 task file already healed. A full `repoos check` then passed, including remote validation of all 708 test files and all local project checks.

## Work and rationale

I checked the live handoff status and current task branch before making changes. The latest failure named the `ignores a marker left behind by an earlier turn` case and timed out waiting for the fake agent turn to end after 45 seconds. I used the focused Vitest filter to rerun precisely that case. It passed, finishing in 2.7 seconds, and the rest of the file was skipped by the filter. This indicates the reported timeout was transient; there was no reproducible code defect to fix in that test.

I also checked `repoos landable 1098`. The previous #1075 bookkeeping conflict had been resolved by the managed RepoOS handoff repair: the branch is clean and task scoped, and main can merge it. The only merge warning is the expected conflict in #1098's own task file, which close-out resolves from main.

To verify beyond the isolated case, I ran the full `repoos check`. Remote validation built the branch and ran all 708 test files: 9,468 tests passed and 14 were skipped. The separate boot timing pass also passed both tests. The remote rendered contrast audit and browser smoke test passed. Local staleness, lockfile, dependency, formatting, lint, build, CSS, contrast, artifact, task-asset, and UI smoke checks passed. User docs and landing builds passed, as did Telegram manager build and all 31 Telegram manager tests. The final check reported no failed steps.

## Approaches tried

I first reran the exact reported timeout test to distinguish a transient timing failure from a repeatable regression. It passed locally. I then ran the full RepoOS check, rather than relying only on the focused test, to cover the remote validation gate that had failed in an earlier handoff message and the repository's complete test and browser checks.

## Challenges and blockers

The full remote check took about 13 minutes, including build and test execution, followed by the browser gates and local checks. The remote test output included existing Vue warnings and expected stderr from tests that deliberately simulate errors; these did not correspond to failed tests. No blocker remains.

## Key learnings

A timeout should be treated as a real defect only if it reproduces or the complete gate exposes a failure. Here, the targeted case finished quickly on rerun, and the complete remote test suite also passed. The handoff repair had already removed the foreign task bookkeeping, so no manual branch edits or changes to another task's file were needed.
